properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean foundation composed of Lower Carboniferous sandstones and siltstones over basaltic volcanic bedrock. Superstructure lithics dominated by local Craigleith and Hailes pale buff-to-grey quartz-arenite sandstone. Bedding laid with historic non-hydraulic lime mortar and fine quartz sand aggregate.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Matures stands along boundary: *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) and *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime). Late September phenology displaying full dense canopy with peripheral chlorosis, early ochre-yellow leaf edge discoloration, and initial leaf fall revealing structural limb branching.

properties.architectural_summary:
Left: Victorian residential terrace townhouse; three storeys over basement, planar ashlar facade, projecting canted three-light bay windows, molded stone cornices, and rectangular sash-and-case fenestration.
Center: Gothic Revival church featuring a square crenellated bell tower with corner pinnacles, stepped stone buttresses, pitched slate nave roof, and pointed-arch lancet windows with stone tracery.
Ground: Planarized asphalt roadway bounded by dressed whinstone kerbs, sandstone retaining plinth wall, and garden perimeter railings.
